No pinned commit SHA obtained this run — direct fetch of github.com/0xOstium was blocked by allowlist. Deployment artifact files (run-latest.json, etc.) not walked.
Protocol operates on a single chain (Arbitrum One). No multi-chain enumeration required. All 15 addresses are on Arbitrum One (chainId 42161).

No factory pattern surfaced in the named contract list. Core contracts are individually deployed (trading, vault, storage, price router, etc.). No factory enumeration required. PairsStorage may act as a registry for trading pairs but is not a child-spawning factory in the Uniswap sense.

On-chain reads (owner(), Safe membership, implementation slots) could not be performed this run because direct arbiscan.io fetch was allowlist-blocked and defipunkd surfacer URLs require pre-pinned addresses. Those addresses are now recorded and the next run inherits them as fetchable surfacers.

protocol_metadata.about: Ostium is a non-custodial decentralized perpetual futures exchange deployed on Arbitrum One that lets users trade perpetual contracts on real-world assets including stocks, ETFs, commodities (gold, oil), forex pairs, indices, and crypto with up to 200x leverage, settling entirely in USDC. Users deposit USDC into self-custodied wallets and interact directly with on-chain smart contracts; liquidity providers deposit USDC into an OLP vault that acts as the counterparty and earns yield from trading fees and funding rates. The protocol uses a two-layer architecture with on-chain settlement contracts and an off-chain hedging layer (partnered with Jump and others) to manage real-world asset price exposure; prices are sourced via a custom price router with Chainlink keeper-style upkeep contracts.
